relationships.subject: AM630
relationships.evidence_quote: The intraperitoneal (3 mg/kg) and subplantar (90 µg) administration of the CB2R antagonist AM630 reversed the mechanical (Figure 3A,D) and cold antiallodynic actions (Figure 3C,F)

relationships.subject: JWH-133
relationships.evidence_quote: JWH-133, given intraperitoneally (1–50 mg/kg) and subplantarly (5–150 µg) dose-dependently inhibited the allodynia and hyperalgesia generated by CCI

relationships.subject: hydrogen sulfide
relationships.evidence_quote: thus supporting the positive interaction between H<sub>2</sub>S and CB2R

relationships.subject: GYY4137
relationships.evidence_quote: Both H2S donors increased the NRF2 expression in the vHIP (Figure 7F; p < 0.001, one-way ANOVA), avoided the downregulation of HO-1 in PFC (Figure 6G; p < 0.001, one-way ANOVA) and increased its expression in the vHIP

relationships.subject: DADS
relationships.evidence_quote: Sciatic nerve injury enhanced the expression of p-IKBα in PFC (Figure 6B; p < 0.001; one-way ANOVA) and PAG (Figure 8B; p < 0.001; one-way ANOVA) and DADS, as well as GYY4137, reversed these effects.

key_findings: H2S donors DADS and GYY4137 enhanced the antinociceptive effect of the CB2R agonist JWH-133 in CCI mice, and AM630 reversed high-dose H2S donor analgesia.
H2S donors normalized p-IKBα and BDNF changes, maintained CB2R levels and activated Nrf2/HO-1 in PFC, vHIP and/or PAG.
